method: AI review of each remaining difference between the frozen HTML and plain-text section bodies. All twelve books and 487 section numbers agree. This is a comparison of two formats of the same edition, not an independent historical witness.
comparison_rules: For audit copies only, exclude translator notes and illustration captions, collapse whitespace, remove underscore emphasis markers, and equate double hyphens with em dashes. The publication source bytes are never normalized.

differences.reason: HTML has a space after the dash before having; the plain text does not.
HTML reads enioyment where the plain text reads enjoyment. Preserve the selected plain-text edition.
The closing uncertainty marker differs: plain text has ... +. while HTML has ...+.
Plain text uses bracketed Greek transliterations; HTML uses Greek characters and has f where the plain text has of.
Plain text has a triple hyphen before a thing; HTML has a space. Do not repair the source punctuation.
HTML adds a period after stupid that is absent from the plain text.
Greek is transliterated in the plain text and printed in Greek characters in HTML; HTML also adds a space before the following period.
HTML has a space before the closing uncertainty marker; plain text does not.
Plain text includes And other things of the same kind. after the verse quotation; HTML omits that sentence.
The cross-reference reads v. 16. 30 in plain text and v. 16, 30 in HTML.
HTML has a space between an ellipsis and the following footnote reference; plain text does not.
